author: ericataylor2347
caption: Let’s color correct and remember less is more. Correctors are usually very concentrated pigments and it’s not necessary to use a lot. Especially on maturing undereyes that have thinned and have texture, lines and wrinkles. 1. Make sure eye is prepped - I used glow 1 balm 2. Correct inner and outer corners and only areas that are darker 3. Place concealer that is skin tone in the middle to blend and correct- this is new Natasha Denona B2 4. Use soft brush to buff - I actually used it cosmetics cream blush brush 5. Pat in with finger tips to press in and remove excess at same time and let’s GO #undereyebags #concealer #corrector #makeup

author: lipstickperfectionist
caption: Under-eye bags don't need MORE concealer... they need the right layers. The product I’m using is linked in the orange cart below, it’s called “CANDLELIGHT” it’s a cream eyeshadow that doubles as a color corrector and lid primer. The trick is color correct first, conceal second, foundation last.  That peach tone helps neutralize the blue/darkness so you can use LESS concealer and still get a smoother, more skin-like finish, especially on mature under eyes. And pleaseeee stop piling thick concealer on the whole area. Thin + creamy + strategic wins. This video is for women over 40 looking for makeup tips for under-eye bags, dark circles, mature skin, color correcting and concealer that doesn't look heavy or cakey.
